notes.text: Vanity — Idols. Vain - Fools; senseless as the stocks and stones that they made their idols of.

Neither — They never concerned themselves about what God had done for them, which should have engaged them to cleave to him. Of drought - Where they had no water but by miracle. Death - Bringing forth nothing that might support life, therefore nothing but death could be expected; and besides, yielding so many venomous creatures, as many enemies that they went in continual danger of. No man dwelt - As having in it no accommodation for travelers, much less for habitation.
My land — Consecrated to my name; by your idols and many other abominations.

They — They that should have taught others, knew as little as they, or regarded as little, who are said here to handle the law, the priests and Levites, who were the ordinary teachers of the law. Pastors - Either teachers, or kings and princes. Prophets - They that should have taught the people the true worship of God, were themselves worshippers of Baal.

Plead — By his judgments, and by his prophets, as he did with their fathers, that they may be left without excuse. Children - God often visits the iniquities of the parents upon the children, when they imitate their parents.

Of Chittim — All the isles in the Mediterranean sea, with the neighbouring coasts; for the Hebrew call all people, that separated from them by the sea, islanders, because they came to them by shipping. Kedar - Arabia that lay east-southeast of Judea, as Chittim did more north or northwest; go from north to south, east to west, and make the experiment; look to Chittim the most civilized, or Kedar the most barbarous, yet neither have changed their gods.
Their glory — The true God, who was their glory; and who always did them good, giving them cause to glory in him.

O ye heavens — A pathetical expression, intimating that it is such a thing, that the very inanimate creatures, could they be sensible of it, would be astonished. Be desolate - Lose your brightness, as the sun seemed to do when Christ suffered.

Of living waters — A metaphor taken from springs, called living, because they never cease, or intermit; such had God's care and kindness been over them. Cisterns - Either their idols, which are empty vain things, that never answer expectation, or the Assyrians, and Egyptians. Indeed all other supports, that are trusted to besides God, are but broken vessels.

glossa.text: *Israel. ((ID.))* Both names are set down, Jacob and Israel, not according to the two and the ten tribes, but according to the whole people, since Jacob himself was afterwards called Israel.

*What have your fathers found.* God speaks of an offence committed by the fathers, not because the sins of the fathers are imputed to the sons, but because the sons, having the likeness of their fathers, are punished both for their own crime and for their parents'. For the sake of the holy fathers God has mercy on the sons.
*Neither did man dwell. ((ID.))* He who is ever hastening to greater things, etc., *as far as* but a struggle, and an uncertain issue of things to come.
*And I brought you in,* as though he should say: In return for the labour of a most hard journey, etc., *as far as* and we make his inheritance abominable.

*Cethim. ((ID.))* Cethim, that is, either of Italy or of the western parts, because near to Judaea is the island of Cyprus, in which there is a city of this name, whence Zeno the prince of the Stoics.

*And consider. ((ID.))* We can say this against those who follow vices with greater zeal than virtues, to whom it is said: *I speak a human thing, because of the infirmity of your flesh; for as you have yielded your members to serve uncleanness and iniquity unto iniquity ((Rom. VI))*, etc.

*My people.* Like the anthropophormitae, who, taking occasion from this testimony: *Let us make man to our image and likeness ((Gen. I))*, stubbornly contend that the boundless and simple substance of the Godhead is composed of our lineaments and of a human shaping.
*Be astonished, O ye heavens. ((ID.))* The Seventy: The heaven was astonished, etc., *as far as* and both the heavens and the heaven are called by the same name, as Thebae, Athenae.

*They have forsaken me.* I who gave the commandment, saying: *I am the Lord thy God, who brought thee out of the land of Egypt.* And according to that which in the same place is written: *Let there be no strange gods before me,* in whose stead he followed after devils.

*The fountain of living water. ((ID.))* A fountain is perpetual and has living waters. Cisterns and pools are filled from torrents and troubled waters by the rains.
*He rejoiceth in God.* Asaph, having set before himself the image of a certain solemnity, stirs up the elect to the festival.

notes.text: Brotherly love is explained in the following verses.

Some — Abraham and Lot. Have entertained angels unawares - So may an unknown guest, even now, be of more worth than he appears, and may have angels attending him, though unseen. Gen. xviii, 2; Gen. xix, 1.

Remember — In your prayers, and by your help. Them that are in bonds, as being bound with them - Seeing ye are members one of another. And them that suffer, as being yourselves in the body - And consequently liable to the same.

Marriage is honourable in, or for all sorts of men, clergy as well as laity: though the Romanists teach otherwise. And the bed undefiled — Consistent with the highest purity; though many spiritual writers, so called, say it is only licensed whoredom. But whoremongers and adulterers God will judge - Though they frequently escape the sentence of men.
He — God. Hath said - To all believers, in saying it to Jacob, Joshua, and Solomon. Gen. xxviii, 15; Josh. i, 5; 1 Chr xxviii, 20.
Psalm cxviii, 6.
Remember them — Who are now with God, considering the happy end of their conversation on earth.
Men may die; but Jesus Christ, yea, and his gospel, is the same from everlasting to everlasting.

glossa.text: *Charity.* From this place the Apostle instructs morally, as if he should say: Because charity is to be had, let it remain in you, and *be not forgetful of hospitality. For by this certain ones have lain hid,* as Lot, not knowing that they were angels, yet knowing who was in them.
*As though bound together with them,* that is, as you would wish help to be given to you if you were bound, or labouring.

*Let your manners be.* After the Hebrews had lost their own goods, they wished to gather again: which the Apostle forbids. But lest they should say: What if necessaries should fail? he subjoins a consolation. *Without covetousness.* The covetous man is he who is tenacious in giving, greedy in receiving. *I will not leave thee.* This God says to everyone that hopes in him, as to Josue, so he is with us, *that we may confidently say,* etc. *Nor forsake.* He would be forsaken who should perish of hunger: but because this is not so, let not a man be greedy.
*I will not fear,* etc. Every adversary is a man, even the devil, who is a man from his office, namely in that he deceives man.
*Be mindful,* etc. Because it is long to speak of each one, he admonishes them to follow their masters.

*Jesus Christ,* etc. This pertains to the sentence above, where he testified that God had said: *I will not leave thee, nor forsake thee.* For it could seem to them that this promise pertained to Josue only, to which he answers, that he will help us also as he helped him. As if: It is not to be doubted, because he who yesterday, that is in the past, helped Josue, today, that is in the present, helps, and will help those to come throughout all ages.

glossa.text: *And a king is today.* Power and riches cannot prolong life. A limit is set which cannot be passed over. The pleasantness of the flesh shall be turned into rottenness and stenches, and at last into worms. But mystically, the man who lives in sins and does not come to his senses shall die an eternal death; and he shall not escape the devil, the old serpent, and his beasts, that is, the demons.

*The beginning of pride.* For there is no greater apostasy than for a creature to withdraw from the Creator, which is deservedly ascribed to pride. For it is pride if a creature wishes to be made equal to the Creator. This was to the devil and to man the beginning of perdition: whence, *For pride is the beginning of all sin.* Although elsewhere it is said: *The desire of money is the root of all evils ((I Tim. VI))*. There is no covetousness without pride, for no man is proud unless he is covetous, and conversely. Of pride are born heresies, schisms, detractions, envy, wordiness, boasting, contentions and the like, which proceed from covetousness. But covetousness makes men gluttonous, intemperate, drunken, fornicators and the like, who cannot be without pride. Let us therefore beware of covetousness and pride, not two evils, but one from which all draw their beginning.

notes.text: Generation — The posterity.
Righteousness — The fruit or reward of his righteousness, which is God's blessing upon his estate.
Darkness — In the troubles and calamities of life. He - The upright man.

Lendeth — Gives freely to some, and lends to others according to the variety of their conditions. Affairs - His domestick affairs. Discretion - Not getting his estate unjustly, nor casting it away prodigally, nor yet withholding it from such as need it.
Moved — Though he may for a season be afflicted, yet he shall not be eternally destroyed.
Evil tidings — At the report of approaching calamities.

Dispersed — His goods, freely and liberally. Righteousness - His liberality, or the reward of it. Ever - What he gives is not lost, but indeed is the only part of his estate, which will abide with him to all eternity.

The desire — Either of the misery of good men; or of his own constant prosperity. We are here exhorted to praise God, ver. 1-3. Particularly for his glory and greatness, ver. 4, 5 And for his grace and goodness, ver. 6-9.

glossa.text: *Blessed is the man.* ((CASS.)) Here the Psalmist shows, after the deliverance, etc., *as far as* thirdly he affirms that adverse things befall the ungodly. *That feareth the Lord.* The fear of the world makes men wretched, but the fear of God makes a man desire those things whereby he is blessed. *In the commandments.* This the fear of God does, that he should will. And he says not "he shall do," etc., *as far as* and *the earthly habitation presseth down the mind that museth upon many things.*

*Mighty.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Behold the rewards of that blessed man. *His seed.* That is, the reward of a good work; *Shall be mighty upon earth,* not upon this earth, where he is a laughing-stock, but upon the heavenly. Or even here in this present time, wherein it is less seen. *Seed,* the works of mercy, whence comes the everlasting harvest. *Mighty,* because with a very small thing, even as with a great one, the kingdom of heaven is bought. *The generation.* Not of the flesh, but of imitation. Or the works of the upright. *The upright* are they who resist not the Father when he corrects, and who believe him when he promises, and who believe not that their works have perished when no requital is made them in time. For there are those who do those good things while hoping here for a reward from God, or wishing to please men, which is not the blessed man: and yet,

*Glory and wealth in his house.* That is, in the secret of the heart, where he dwells with the hope of eternal life, where holy riches and eternal glory are laid up. *Justice.* This is his glory, these are his riches, which nevertheless he has from God. *It remaineth for ever.* As it were, he is not blessed for a time.
*There hath risen up.* ((CASS.)) Secondly he treats of the coming of the Lord, etc., *as far as* that he may fortify it beforehand with firm allegations and assertions in the judgment. Or,
*He sheweth mercy.* ((ID.)) He who gives to the needy; *He lendeth,* he who grants a loan, to receive afterwards as much again.

*His heart is ready to hope in the Lord, his heart is strengthened, it remaineth,* etc. ((AUG.)) It is plain therefore that this man seeks not his own things, but the things which are Christ's; he bears labours patiently, he awaits the promises with confidence. ((CASS.)) Or, if any man threatens evils, he fears not, but is ready.

*He hath distributed.* He hopes not to fear, because he has distributed. *He hath given to the poor.* ((AUG.)) Behold, this man was buying what he did not see, but that other was keeping a treasure for him in heaven, who vouchsafes to hunger and to thirst in the poor upon earth. *His justice remaineth for ever and ever.* ((CASS.)) He gave what was his own, and lived justly and godly; or, he who gives what is his own works justice. *His horn shall be exalted in glory.* Because he is humble here, there he shall have power.

*The sinner shall see.* ((ID.)) Thirdly he affirms that contrary things befall the ungodly. By the good things of the blessed he exhorts, by the evils of the enemies he terrifies, and this psalm is an instructor of the faithful.

*He shall be angry, he shall gnash with his teeth and pine away, the desire of the wicked shall perish,* saying: *What hath pride profited us, and the boasting of riches? ((Sap. V))*

registers.label: Spare
lines: You forsook the fountain of living water for cracked cisterns that hold nothing.
Bring us back to the spring that never fails.
When you are invited, take the lowest place, and the host will say, friend, come up higher.
We come not to be honored, but to be welcomed.
Open wide your mouth, and God will fill it; show your love to the stranger at the door.
Some have welcomed angels without knowing.
Come, take your place at the table and worship.
Friend, come up higher. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture a crowded banquet, everyone angling for the good seats — and Jesus says, take the lowest place, down at the end, and wait.
Friend, come up higher.
For the host walks the room and finds you there, and instead of being asked to move down, you hear your name and a hand on your shoulder.
Friend, come up higher.
This is the God who fills the open mouth with the finest wheat, who keeps the door open to the stranger and the angel unawares.
Friend, come up higher.
So leave the cracked cisterns and the scramble for honor. There is a place set for you, and a voice already calling you in.
Friend, come up higher. Thanks be to God!

lines: Take the lowest seat and wait.
